passage: On the kitchen floor sat four toddlers, each with a plastic box they could not open. Swati twisted the lid, pulled it, banged it on the tiles and poked at its edge with one finger. Every move lasted a few seconds and was dropped when nothing gave. Vidya had seen her father unscrew his tiffin box that morning. She copied the turning motion of his wrist on a small pack of raisins, but she turned it in the opposite direction, so the cover stayed put. Sarika's lid would not budge either. Her face went red, she hurled the box towards the wall and screamed, and there was no more trying after that. Little Rohan had once popped a box open by pressing its corner, purely by chance. Now he pressed at each lid's corner, and was baffled when a bottle with a screw cap did nothing at all.

qa.q: What did Vidya copy from her father?
qa.a: She copied the twisting motion of his wrist on the lid.

qa.q: How does Sarika's reaction differ from Swati's, and what did each do with the lid?
qa.a: Swati kept trying different moves for a few seconds each, so she kept exploring. Sarika's strong feeling made her throw the box and scream, which ended any trying.

qa.q: What was Rohan probably feeling when the screw-top bottle did nothing?
qa.a: He was puzzled, since pressing the corner had worked on earlier boxes and now it did not.

qa.q: How could a caregiver support Sarika when the lid will not open?
qa.a: A caregiver could stay near, name the upset feeling calmly, and show one way to try again or help with the first turn, so the trying can start again. 🙂

grounding: Four toddlers try to open a plastic box by trial and error, imitation, giving way to frustration, and repeating a move that once worked.
